SELECT run_id,p99_ttft_ms,p99_itl_ms,gpu_hours,completed_requests FROM provenance.llm_run_summary WHERE run_id LIKE 'planner:week%'; -> planner:week_fc_p90 = 518.6063450234815 GPU-h, TTFT p99 651.1395, ITL p99 6.4056, 749601 req. Denominator, THREE independent legitimate derivations: (a) published operands 518.6/537.4 = 0.96501675; (b) span x 4 GPUs, SELECT span_s, span_s/3600.0*4 FROM provenance.windows WHERE window_name='aggregate' -> 483659.8 s -> 537.3997778 GPU-h, ratio = 0.96502895; (c) full-trace static pro-rated, SELECT gpu_hours FROM provenance.llm_run_summary WHERE run_id='a13:ft_llm_static' -> 672.0093014234247 over the 604799.7 s fulltrace span, pro-rated 672.0093014*483659.8/604799.7 = 537.40748 GPU-h, ratio = 0.96501512. ALL THREE give 0.9650 to four decimals -- i.e. the ratio lands EXACTLY on the 2-dp rounding tie point, and the three defensible denominators disagree at the 3e-5 level, which is larger than the distance from the tie. The value is therefore not determinable to better than 0.9650, and both 0.96 (truncation / round-half-even) and 0.97 (round-half-up) are obtainable under ordinary conventions. The first pass's argument that 'the paragraph's companions are rounded half-up (625.27->625, 641.08->641, 1.163->1.16, 1.193->1.19)' is void: NONE of those is a boundary case -- every one is plain round-to-nearest with no tie -- so they carry zero evidence about how the author breaks a tie. Decisive corroboration: the SAME ratio at the SAME precision, printed next to its own operands, is CONFIRMED in the already-adversarially-reviewed closedloop chapter (verified/closedloop.json line 374: 'Ratio 0.965 rounds to 0.96', verdict CONFIRMED), and closedloop.tex:375 is NOT on the ADJUDICATION edit list. Changing tese.tex:68 to 0.97 would leave closedloop.tex:373-375 printing '518.6 ... 537.4 ... (0.96x)' and would manufacture a cross-chapter inconsistency where none exists. Semantics are unaffected either way ('slightly below', 'near-break-even').
